newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Southern Glass set to open US$120 million project.
newsitem.headline: Southern Glass set to open US$120 million project.

text.p: Shenzhen-based China Southern Glass Holdings Co Ltd said on Friday that its US$120 million super-thin float glass project would begin partial operations next month.
The line is slated to turn out 120,000 tonnes of float glass annually, a company spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman told the China Securities Bulletin the project should generate annual earnings of about 100 million yuan on sales of more than 500 million yuan when fully operational in early 1997.
The super-thin float glass is expected to become the company's main source of profits by the end of the century, she added.

The Shenzhen-listed company said in its interim report that it posted net earnings of 70.16 million yuan in the first half of 1996, down 14.09 percent from the year earlier's level of 81.67 million yuan.
The firm did not state whether the interim results had been compiled under Chinese or international accounting standards.
A company spokesman blamed the lower earnings on sharpening competition in the mainland Chinese market from domestic counterparts.

He also said that Beijing's credit clampdown had dampened demand in the building industry, but added that the central bank's recent cuts in lending rates could spark an upsurge in the sector and in the firm's second-half earnings.
